Figure 1:Two benchmark failure cases.In both panels, the curves show true modelconditionalperformanceas a function of question difficulty.
(a)Measure Mismatch.The benchmark emphasizes easy questions, where the models perform similarly, while the difficulty distribution we care about places more weight on harder questions, where they differ substantially.
Because the benchmark and the target distribution weight the difficulty axis differently, they lead to different conclusions for the same two models.
(b)Coverage Gaps.A model actually improvessubstantiallyover a localized difficulty region. Because the benchmark has no questions in that region, this improvement is not reflected in the observed benchmark score, causing meaningful training progress to be missed.

Figure 2:Overview of our benchmark difficulty estimation and metric calculation pipeline.We collect empirical success rates from multiple LLMs on benchmark items, diagnose the response matrix, fit a 1PL IRT model to estimate item difficulties, perform post-fit IRT diagnostics, and compute two metrics over the normalized difficulty distribution.
Figure 4:Overview ofBenchFill.BenchFilliteratively rewrites parent items into child variants, annotates their difficulties, and updates the memory to guide the next round of gap filling.
